A quadrature encoder can be connected directly to the MCU without external interface logic. However, comparators are normally be used to convert the encoder’s differential outputs to digital signals. This greatly increases noise immunity. The third encoder output which indicate the mechanical zero position, may be connected to the external trigger input and trigger a counter reset.

[Figure 356](#XREF_13085__Figure_43__Example_of_counter_operation_in_encoder_interface_mode_21) gives an example of counter operation, showing count signal generation and direction control. It also shows how input jitter is compensated where both edges are selected. This might occur if the sensor is positioned near to one of the switching points. For this example the configuration is the following:

- CC1S = 01 (TIMx\_CCMR1 register, tim\_ti1fp1 mapped on tim\_ti1).
- CC2S = 01 (TIMx\_CCMR1 register, tim\_ti2fp2 mapped on tim\_ti2).
- CC1P = 0 and CC1NP = 0 (TIMx\_CCER register, tim\_ti1fp1 noninverted, tim\_ti1fp1 = tim\_ti1).
- CC2P = 0 and CC2NP = 0 (TIMx\_CCER register, tim\_ti1fp2 noninverted, tim\_ti1fp2= tim\_ti2).
- SMS = 0011 (TIMx\_SMCR register, both inputs are active on both rising and falling edges).
- CEN = 1 (TIMx\_CR1 register, Counter enabled).
<a id="XREF_13085__Figure_43__Example_of_counter_operation_in_encoder_interface_mode_21"></a>

#### Figure 356. Example of counter operation in encoder interface mode.![](MSv62349V1.svg)

[Figure 357](#XREF_80656__Figure_44__Example_of_counter_operation_in_encoder_interface_mode_21) gives an example of counter behavior when tim\_ti1fp1 polarity is inverted (same configuration as above except CC1P = 1).

<a id="XREF_80656__Figure_44__Example_of_counter_operation_in_encoder_interface_mode_21"></a>

#### Figure 357. Example of encoder interface mode with tim\_ti1fp1 polarity inverted.![](MSv62350V1.svg)

[Figure 358](#XREF_33535__Figure_190__Quadrature_encoder_counting_modes21) shows the timer counter value during a speed reversal, for various counting modes.

<a id="XREF_33535__Figure_190__Quadrature_encoder_counting_modes21"></a>

#### Figure 358. Quadrature encoder counting modes![](MSv62351V1.svg)

The timer, when configured in Encoder Interface mode provides information on the sensor’s current position. Dynamic information can be obtained (speed, acceleration, deceleration) by measuring the period between two encoder events using a second timer configured in capture mode. The output of the encoder which indicates the mechanical zero can be used for this purpose. Depending on the time between two events, the counter can also be read at regular times. This can be done by latching the counter value into a third input capture register if available (then the capture signal must be periodic and can be generated by another timer). When available, it is also possible to read its value through a DMA request.

The IUFREMAP bit in the TIMx\_CR1 register forces a continuous copy of the update interrupt flag (UIF) into the timer counter register’s bit 31 (TIMxCNT[31]). This allows both the counter value and a potential roll-over condition signaled by the UIFCPY flag to be read in an atomic way. It eases the calculation of angular speed by avoiding race conditions caused, for instance, by a processing shared between a background task (counter reading) and an interrupt (update interrupt).

There is no latency between the UIF and UIFCPY flag assertions.

In 32-bit timer implementations, when the IUFREMAP bit is set, bit 31 of the counter is overwritten by the UIFCPY flag upon read access (the counter’s most significant bit is only accessible in write mode).

#### Clock plus direction encoder mode

In addition to the quadrature encoder mode, the timer offers support for other types of encoders.

In the clock plus direction mode shown on [Figure 359](#XREF_50552__Figure_191__Direction_plus_clock_encoder_mode21), the clock is provided on a single line, on tim\_ti2, while the direction is forced using the tim\_ti1 input.

This mode is enabled with the SMS[3:0] bitfield in the TIMx\_SMCR register, as following:

- 1010: x2 mode, the counter is updated on both rising and falling edges of the clock
- 1011: x1 mode, the counter is updated on a single clock edge, as per CC2P bit value: CC2P = 0 corresponds to rising edge sensitivity and CC2P = 1 corresponds to falling edge sensitivity

The polarity of the direction signal on tim\_ti1 is set with the CC1P bit: 0 corresponds to positive polarity (up-counting when tim\_ti1 is high and down-counting when tim\_ti1 is low) and CC1P = 1 corresponds to negative polarity (up-counting when tim\_ti1 is low).

<a id="XREF_50552__Figure_191__Direction_plus_clock_encoder_mode21"></a>

#### Figure 359. Direction plus clock encoder mode![](MSv62352V1.svg)

#### Directional clock encoder mode

In the directional clock mode on [Figure 360](#XREF_55995__Figure_192__Directional_clock_encode_mode21), the clocks are provided on two lines, with a single one at once, depending on the direction, so as to have one up-counting clock line and one down-counting clock line.

This mode is enabled with the SMS[3:0] bitfield in the TIMx\_SMCR register, as following:

- 1100: x2 mode, the counter is updated on both rising and falling edges of any of the two clock line. The CC1P and CC2P bits are coding for the clock idle state. CCxP = 0 corresponds to high-level idle state (refer to [Figure 360](#XREF_55995__Figure_192__Directional_clock_encode_mode21)) and CCxP = 1 corresponds to low-level idle state (refer to [Figure 361](#XREF_26952__Figure_195__Directional_clock_encode_mode_(CC1P_=_CC2P_=_1)21)).
- 1101: x1 mode, the counter is updated on a single clock edge, as per CC1P and CC2P bit value. CCxP = 0 corresponds to falling edge sensitivity and high-level idle state (refer to [Figure 360](#XREF_55995__Figure_192__Directional_clock_encode_mode21)), CCxP = 1 corresponds to rising edge sensitivity and low-level idle state (refer to [Figure 361](#XREF_26952__Figure_195__Directional_clock_encode_mode_(CC1P_=_CC2P_=_1)21)).
<a id="XREF_55995__Figure_192__Directional_clock_encode_mode21"></a>

#### Figure 360. Directional clock encoder mode (CC1P = CC2P = 0)![](MSv62353V1.svg)

<a id="XREF_26952__Figure_195__Directional_clock_encode_mode_(CC1P_=_CC2P_=_1)21"></a>

#### Figure 361. Directional clock encoder mode (CC1P = CC2P = 1)![](MSv62354V1.svg)

#### Index input

The counter can be reset by an index signal coming from the encoder, indicating an absolute reference position. The index signal must be connected to the tim\_etr\_in input. It can be filtered using the digital input filter.

The index functionality is enabled with the IE bit in the TIMX\_ECR register. The IE bit must be set only in encoder mode, when the SMS[3:0] bitfield has the following values: 0001, 0010, 011, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, 1111.

Available encoders are proposed with several options for index pulse conditioning, as per [Figure 362](#XREF_47987__Figure_199__Index_gating_options21):

- gated with A and B: the pulsewidth is 1/4 of one channel period, aligned with both A and B edges
- gated with A (or gated with B): the pulsewidth is 1/2 of one channel period, aligned with the two edges on channel A (resp. channel B)
- ungated: the pulsewidth is up to one channel period, without any alignment to the edges
<a id="XREF_47987__Figure_199__Index_gating_options21"></a>

#### Figure 362. Index gating options![](MSv45765V1.svg)

The circuitry tolerates jitter on index signal, whatever the gating mode, as show on [Figure 363](#XREF_65150__Figure_193_21).

In ungated mode, the signal must be strictly below two encoder periods. If the pulsewidth is greater or equal to two encoder period, the counter is reset multiple times.

<a id="XREF_65150__Figure_193_21"></a>

#### Figure 363. Jittered Index signals![](MSv45766V1.svg)

The timer supports the three gating options identically, without any specific programming needed. It is only necessary to define on which encoder state (for example channel A and channel B state combination) the index must be synchronized, using the IPOS[1:0] bitfield in the TIMx\_ECR register.

The index detection event acts differently depending on counting direction to ensure symmetrical operation during speed reversal:

- The counter is reset during up-counting (DIR bit = 0).
- The counter is set to TIMx\_ARR when down counting.

This allows the index to be generated on the very same mechanical angular position whatever the counting direction. [Figure 364](#XREF_69382_0%5D%13=_1121) shows at which position is the index generated, for a simplistic example (an encoder providing four edges par mechanical rotation).

<a id="XREF_69382_0%5D%13=_1121"></a>

#### Figure 364. Index generation for IPOS[1:0] = 11![](MSv45767V1.svg)

[Figure 365](#XREF_52830__Figure_190__Counter_reading_with_index_gated_on_channel_A21) presents waveforms and corresponding values for IPOS[1:0] = 11. It shows that the instant at which the counter value is forced is automatically adjusted depending on the counting direction:

- Counter set to 0 when encoder state is 11 (ChA = 1, ChB = 1), when up-counting (DIR bit = 0).
- Counter set to TIMx\_ARR when exiting the 11 state, when down-counting (DIR bit = 1).

An interrupt can be issued upon index detection event.

The arrows are indicating on which transition is the index event interrupt generated.

<a id="XREF_52830__Figure_190__Counter_reading_with_index_gated_on_channel_A21"></a>

#### Figure 365. Counter reading with index gated on channel A (IPOS[1:0] = 11)![](MSv45768V1.svg)

[Figure 366.](#XREF_31732__Figure_191__Counter_reading_with_index_ungated21) presents waveforms and corresponding values for the ungated mode. The arrows are indicating on which transition is the index event generated.

<a id="XREF_31732__Figure_191__Counter_reading_with_index_ungated21"></a>

#### Figure 366. Counter reading with index ungated (IPOS[1:0] = 00)![](MSv45769V1.svg)

[Figure 367.](#XREF_69040__Figure_192_21) shows how the ‘gated on A & B’ mode is handled, for various pulse alignment scenario. The arrows are indicating on which transition is the index event generated.

<a id="XREF_69040__Figure_192_21"></a>

#### Figure 367. Counter reading with index gated on channel A and B![](MSv45770V1.svg)

[Figure 368](#XREF_73550__Figure_194__Narrow_index_pulse_following_a_detection_on_Channel_B21) and [Figure 369](#XREF_42832__Figure_196__Counter_reset_Narrow_index_pulse_(closer_view)21) detail the case where the subsequent index pulse may be narrower than one quarter of the encoder clock period.

<a id="XREF_73550__Figure_194__Narrow_index_pulse_following_a_detection_on_Channel_B21"></a>

#### Figure 368. narrow index pulse (IPOS[1:0] = 11)Encoder mode behavior in case of ![](MSv45771V1.svg)

<a id="XREF_42832__Figure_196__Counter_reset_Narrow_index_pulse_(closer_view)21"></a>

#### Figure 369. Counter reset Narrow index pulse (closer view, ARR = 0x07)![](MSv45772V1.svg)

[Figure 370](#XREF_92120__Figure_197__Index_behavior_in_x1_and_x2_mode21) shows how the index is managed in x1 and x2 modes.

<a id="XREF_92120__Figure_197__Index_behavior_in_x1_and_x2_mode21"></a>

#### Directional index sensitivity

The IDIR[1:0] bitfield in the TIMx\_ECR register allows the index to be active only in a selected counting direction.

[Figure 371](#XREF_24064__Figure_197__Directional_index_sensitivity21) shows the relationship between index and counter reset events, depending on IDIR[1:0] value.

**Note:**

The IDR[1:0] bitfield must be written when IE bit is reset (index mode disabled).

**Note:**

The directional index sensitivity is not supported in clock + direction mode. When SMS[3:0] = 1010 or 1011, the IDIR[1:0] must be set to 00.

<a id="XREF_24064__Figure_197__Directional_index_sensitivity21"></a>

#### Figure 371. Directional index sensitivity![](MSv45774V1.svg)

#### Special first index event management

The FIDX bit in the TIMx\_ECR register allows the index to be taken only once, as shown on [Figure 372](#XREF_10344__Figure_198__Counter_reset_as_function_of_FIDX_bit_setting21). Once the first index has arrived, any subsequent index is ignored. If needed, the circuitry can be rearmed by writing the FIDX bit to 0 and setting it again to 1.

**Note:**

When FIDX = 1, the index can be issued twice (IDXF flag set) if the direction changes at position 0 (index active).

<a id="XREF_10344__Figure_198__Counter_reset_as_function_of_FIDX_bit_setting21"></a>

#### Figure 372. Counter reset as function of FIDX bit setting![MSv45775V1](MSv45775V1.svg)

#### Index management in nonquadrature mode

[Figure 373](#XREF_81356__Figure_201__Index_behavior_in_clock_+_direction_mode21) and [Figure 374](#XREF_24012__Figure_202__Index_behavior_in_directional_clock_mode21) detail how the index is managed in directional clock mode and clock plus direction mode, when the SMS[3:0] bitfield is equal to 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101.

For both of these modes, the index sensitivity is set with the IPOS[0] bit as following:

- IPOS[0] = 0: Index is detected on clock low level
- IPOS[0] = 1: Index is detected on clock high level

The IPOS[1] bit is not-significant.

<a id="XREF_81356__Figure_201__Index_behavior_in_clock_+_direction_mode21"></a>

#### Figure 373. Index behavior in clock + direction mode, IPOS[0] = 1![](MSv62355V1.svg)

<a id="XREF_24012__Figure_202__Index_behavior_in_directional_clock_mode21"></a>

#### Figure 374. Index behavior in directional clock mode, IPOS[0] = 1![](MSv62356V1.svg)

#### Encoder error management

For encoder configurations where two quadrature signals are available, it is possible to detect transition errors. The reading on the two inputs corresponds to a 2-bit gray code which can be represented as a state diagram, on [Figure 375.](#XREF_76719__Figure_2__State_diagram_for_quadrature_encoded_signals21). A single bit is expected to change at once. An erroneous transition sets the TERRF interrupt flag in the TIMx\_SR status register. A transition error interrupt is generated if the TERRIE bit is set in the TIMx\_DIER register.

<a id="XREF_76719__Figure_2__State_diagram_for_quadrature_encoded_signals21"></a>

#### Figure 375. State diagram for quadrature encoded signals![](MSv45779V1.svg)

For encoder having an index signal, it is possible to detect abnormal operation resulting in an excess of pulses per revolution. An encoder with N pulses per revolution provides 4xN counts per revolution. The index signal resets the counter every 4xN clock periods.

If the counter value is incremented from TIMx\_ARR to 0 or decremented from 0 to TIMxARR value without any index event, this is reported as an index position error.

The overflow threshold is programmed using the TIMx\_ARR register. A 1000 lines encoder results in a counter value being between 0 and 3999 (in 4x reading mode). The overflow detection threshold must be programmed by setting TIMx\_ARR = 3999 + 1 = 4000.

The error assertion is delayed to the transition 0 to 1 when in up-counting. This is cope with narrow index pulses in gated A and B mode, as shown on [Figure 376](#XREF_65387__Figure_211__Error_detection21).

<a id="XREF_65387__Figure_211__Error_detection21"></a>

#### Figure 376. Up-counting encoder error detection![](MSv62357V1.svg)

In down-counting mode, the detection is conditioned by a preliminary transition from 1 to 0. This is to cope with narrow index pulses in gated A and B mode, as shown on [Figure 377](#XREF_61725__Figure_212__Encode_error_detection21), to avoid any false error detection in case the encoder dithers between TIMx\_ARR and 0 immediately after the index detection.

<a id="XREF_61725__Figure_212__Encode_error_detection21"></a>

#### Figure 377. Down-counting encode error detection![](MSv62358V1.svg)

An index error sets the IERRF interrupt flag in the TIMx\_SR status register. An index error interrupt is generated if the IERRIE bit is set in the TIMx\_DIER register.

#### Functional encoder interrupts

The following interrupts are also available in encoder mode

- Direction change: any change of the counting direction in encoder mode causes the DIR bit in the TIMx\_CR1 register to toggle. The direction change sets the DIRF interrupt flag in the TIMx\_SR status register. A direction change interrupt is generated if the DIRIE bit is set in the TIMx\_DIER register.
- Index event: the index event sets the IDXF interrupt flag in the TIMx\_SR status register. An index interrupt is generated if the IDXIE bit is set in the TIMx\_DIER register.

#### Slave mode selection preload for run-time encoder mode update

It may be necessary to switch from one encoder mode to another during run-time. This is typically done at high-speed to decrease the update interrupt rate, by switching from x4 to x2 to x1 mode, as shown on [Figure 378](#XREF_73988__Figure_195__Encoder_mode_change_with_preload_enable21).

For this purpose, the SMS[3:0] bit can be preloaded. This is enabled by setting the SMSPE enable bit in the TIMx\_SMCR register. The trigger for the transfer from SMS[3:0] preload to active value can be selected with the SMSPS bit in the TIMx\_SMCR register.

- SMSPS = 0: the transfer is triggered by the update event (UEV) occurring when the counter overflows when upcounting, and underflows when downcounting. This mode must be used only when index is disabled (bit IE = 0).
- SMSPS = 1: the transfer is triggered by the index event.
<a id="XREF_73988__Figure_195__Encoder_mode_change_with_preload_enable21"></a>

#### Figure 378. Encoder mode change with preload transferred on update (SMSPS = 0)![](MSv45781V1.svg)

#### Encoder clock output

The encoder mode operating principle is not perfectly suited for high-resolution velocity measurements, at low speed, as it requires a relatively long integration time to have a sufficient number of clock edges and a precise measurement.

At low speed, a better solution is to do an edge-to-edge clock period measurement. This can be achieved using a slave timer. The timer can output the encoder clock information on the tim\_trgo output. The slave timer can then perform a period measurement and provide velocity information for each and every encoder clock edge.

This mode is enabled by setting the MMS[3:0] bitfield to 1000, in the TIMx\_CR2 register.It is valid for the following SMS[3:0] values: 0001, 0010, 0011, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, 1111. Any other SMS[3:0] code is not allowed and may lead to unexpected behavior.

### 29.3.26 Direction bit output

Its is possible to output a direction signal out of the timer, on the tim\_oc3n and tim\_oc4 output signals (copy of the DIR bit in the TIMx\_CR1 register). This is achieved by setting the OC3M[3:0] or the OC4M[3:0] bitfield to 1011 in the TIMx\_CCMR2 register.

This feature can be used for monitoring the counting direction (or rotation direction) in encoder mode, or to have a signal indicating the up/down phases in center-aligned PWM mode.

### 29.3.27 UIF bit remapping

The IUFREMAP bit in the TIMx\_CR1 register forces a continuous copy of the update interrupt flag UIF into the timer counter register’s bit 31 (TIMxCNT[31]). This allows both the counter value and a potential roll-over condition signaled by the UIFCPY flag to be read in an atomic way. In particular cases, it can ease the calculations by avoiding race conditions, caused for instance by a processing shared between a background task (counter reading) and an interrupt (update interrupt).

There is no latency between the UIF and UIFCPY flags assertion.

### 29.3.28 Timer input XOR function

The TI1S bit in the TIMx\_CR2 register, allows the input filter of channel 1 to be connected to the output of an XOR gate, combining the three input pins tim\_ti1, tim\_ti2 and tim\_ti3.

The XOR output can be used with all the timer input functions such as trigger or input capture. It is convenient to measure the interval between edges on two input signals, as per [Figure 379](#XREF_28669__Figure_54__Measuring_time_interval_between_edges_on_2_signals21).

<a id="XREF_28669__Figure_54__Measuring_time_interval_between_edges_on_2_signals21"></a>

#### Figure 379. Measuring time interval between edges on three signals![](MSv75854V1.svg)

### 29.3.29 Interfacing with Hall sensors

This is done using the advanced-control timers to generate PWM signals to drive the motor and another timer TIMx referred to as “interfacing timer” in [Figure 380](#XREF_55655__Figure_56__Example_of_Hall_Sensors_Interface21). The “interfacing timer” captures the three timer input pins (tim\_ti1, tim\_ti2 and tim\_ti3) connected through a XOR to the tim\_ti1 input channel (selected by setting the TI1S bit in the TIMx\_CR2 register).

The slave mode controller is configured in reset mode; the slave input is tim\_ti1f\_ed. Thus, each time one of the three inputs toggles, the counter restarts counting from 0. This creates a time base triggered by any change on the Hall inputs.

On the “interfacing timer”, capture/compare channel 1 is configured in capture mode, capture signal is tim\_trc (See [Figure 323](#XREF_21775__channel_1_Input_stage)21)). The captured value, which corresponds to the time elapsed between two changes on the inputs, gives information about motor speed.

The “interfacing timer” can be used in output mode to generate a pulse which changes the configuration of the channels of the advanced-control timer (by triggering a COM event). The advanced-control timer is used to generate PWM signals to drive the motor. To do this, the interfacing timer channel must be programmed so that a positive pulse is generated after a programmed delay (in output compare or PWM mode). This pulse is sent to the advanced-control timer through the tim\_trgo output.

In this example the user wants to change the PWM configuration of the advanced-control timer after a programmed delay each time a change occurs on the Hall inputs connected to one of the TIMx timers.

- Configure three timer inputs ORed to the tim\_ti1 input channel by writing the TI1S bit in the TIMx\_CR2 register to 1.
- Program the time base: write the TIMx\_ARR to the max value (the counter must be cleared by the tim\_ti1 change. Set the prescaler to get a maximum counter period longer than the time between two changes on the sensors.
- Program the channel 1 in capture mode (tim\_trc selected): write the CC1S bits in the TIMx\_CCMR1 register to 01. The digital filter can also be programmed if needed.
- Program the channel 2 in PWM 2 mode with the desired delay: write the OC2M bits to 111 and the CC2S bits to 00 in the TIMx\_CCMR1 register.
- Select tim\_oc2ref as trigger output on tim\_trgo: write the MMS bits in the TIMx\_CR2 register to 101.

In the advanced-control timer, the right tim\_itrx input must be selected as trigger input, the timer is programmed to generate PWM signals, the capture/compare control signals are preloaded (CCPC = 1 in the TIMx\_CR2 register) and the COM event is controlled by the trigger input (CCUS = 1 in the TIMx\_CR2 register). The PWM control bits (CCxE, OCxM) are written after a COM event for the next step (this can be done in an interrupt subroutine generated by the rising edge of tim\_oc2ref).

[Figure 380](#XREF_55655__Figure_56__Example_of_Hall_Sensors_Interface21) describes this example.

<a id="XREF_55655__Figure_56__Example_of_Hall_Sensors_Interface21"></a>

#### Figure 380. Example of Hall sensor interface![](MSv62360V1.svg)

<a id="XREF_50306__12_4_19_TIM1_and_external_trigger_synchronization21"></a>

### 29.3.30 Timer synchronization

The TIMx timers are linked together internally for timer synchronization or chaining. Refer to [Section 30.4.23: Timer synchronization](General-purpose_timers_%28TIM2__47_TIM3__47_TIM4__47_TIM5%29.md#XREF_17049__12_4_14_Timer_synchronization41) for details. They can be synchronized in several modes: Reset mode, Gated mode, Trigger mode, Reset + trigger, and gated + reset modes.

#### Slave mode: Reset mode

The counter and its prescaler can be reinitialized in response to an event on a trigger input. Moreover, if the URS bit from the TIMx\_CR1 register is low, an update event UEV is generated. Then all the preloaded registers (TIMx\_ARR, TIMx\_CCRx) are updated.

In the following example, the upcounter is cleared in response to a rising edge on tim\_ti1 input:

- Configure the channel 1 to detect rising edges on tim\_ti1. Configure the input filter duration (in this example, we do not need any filter, so we keep IC1F = 0000). The capture prescaler is not used for triggering, so it does not need to be configured. The CC1S bits select the input capture source only, CC1S = 01 in the TIMx\_CCMR1 register. Write CC1P = 0 and CC1NP = 0 in TIMx\_CCER register to validate the polarity (and detect rising edges only).
- Configure the timer in reset mode by writing SMS = 100 in TIMx\_SMCR register. Select tim\_ti1 as the input source by writing TS = 00101 in TIMx\_SMCR register.
- Start the counter by writing CEN = 1 in the TIMx\_CR1 register.

The counter starts counting on the internal clock, then behaves normally until tim\_ti1 rising edge. When tim\_ti1 rises, the counter is cleared and restarts from 0. In the meantime, the trigger flag is set (TIF bit in the TIMx\_SR register) and an interrupt request, or a DMA request can be sent if enabled (depending on the TIE and TDE bits in TIMx\_DIER register).

The following figure shows this behavior when the autoreload register TIMx\_ARR = 0x36. The delay between the rising edge on tim\_ti1 and the actual reset of the counter is due to the resynchronization circuit on tim\_ti1 input.

#### Figure 381. Control circuit in reset mode![](MSv62361V1.svg)

#### Slave mode: Gated mode

The counter can be enabled depending on the level of a selected input.

In the following example, the upcounter counts only when tim\_ti1 input is low:

- Configure the channel 1 to detect low levels on tim\_ti1. Configure the input filter duration (in this example, we do not need any filter, so we keep IC1F = 0000). The capture prescaler is not used for triggering, so it does not need to be configured. The CC1S bits select the input capture source only, CC1S = 01 in TIMx\_CCMR1 register. Write CC1P = 1 and CC1NP = 0 in TIMx\_CCER register to validate the polarity (and detect low level only).
- Configure the timer in gated mode by writing SMS = 101 in TIMx\_SMCR register. Select tim\_ti1 as the input source by writing TS = 00101 in TIMx\_SMCR register.
- Enable the counter by writing CEN = 1 in the TIMx\_CR1 register (in gated mode, the counter does not start if CEN = 0, whatever is the trigger input level).

The counter starts counting on the internal clock as long as tim\_ti1 is low and stops as soon as tim\_ti1 becomes high. The TIF flag in the TIMx\_SR register is set both when the counter starts or stops.

The delay between the rising edge on tim\_ti1 and the actual stop of the counter is due to the resynchronization circuit on tim\_ti1 input.

#### Figure 382. Control circuit in Gated mode![](MSv62362V1.svg)

#### Slave mode: Trigger mode

The counter can start in response to an event on a selected input.

In the following example, the upcounter starts in response to a rising edge on tim\_ti2 input:

- Configure the channel 2 to detect rising edges on tim\_ti2. Configure the input filter duration (in this example, we do not need any filter, so we keep IC2F = 0000). The capture prescaler is not used for triggering, so it does not need to be configured. The CC2S bits are configured to select the input capture source only, CC2S = 01 in TIMx\_CCMR1 register. Write CC2P = 1 and CC2NP = 0 in TIMx\_CCER register to validate the polarity (and detect low level only).
- Configure the timer in trigger mode by writing SMS = 110 in TIMx\_SMCR register. Select tim\_ti2 as the input source by writing TS = 00110 in TIMx\_SMCR register.

When a rising edge occurs on tim\_ti2, the counter starts counting on the internal clock and the TIF flag is set.

The delay between the rising edge on tim\_ti2 and the actual start of the counter is due to the resynchronization circuit on tim\_ti2 input.

#### Figure 383. Control circuit in trigger mode![](MSv62363V1.svg)

#### Slave mode: Combined reset + trigger mode

In this case, a rising edge of the selected trigger input (tim\_trgi) reinitializes the counter, generates an update of the registers, and starts the counter.

This mode is used for One-pulse mode.

#### Slave mode: Combined gated + reset mode

The counter clock is enabled when the trigger input (tim\_trgi) is high. The counter stops and is reset) as soon as the trigger becomes low. Both start and stop of the counter are controlled.

This mode is used to detect out-of-range PWM signal (duty cycle exceeding a maximum expected value).

#### Slave mode: external clock mode 2 + trigger mode

The external clock mode 2 can be used in addition to another slave mode (except external clock mode 1 and encoder mode). In this case, the tim\_etr\_in signal is used as external clock input, and another input can be selected as trigger input (in reset mode, gated mode or trigger mode). It is recommended not to select tim\_etr\_in as tim\_trgi through the TS bits of TIMx\_SMCR register.

In the following example, the upcounter is incremented at each rising edge of the tim\_etr\_in signal as soon as a rising edge of tim\_ti1 occurs:

1. Configure the external trigger input circuit by programming the TIMx\_SMCR register as follows:
<br>- ETF = 0000: no filter
<br>- ETPS = 00: prescaler disabled
<br>- ETP = 0: detection of rising edges on tim\_etr\_in and ECE = 1 to enable the external clock mode 2.
2. Configure the channel 1 as follows, to detect rising edges on TI:
<br>- IC1F = 0000: no filter.
<br>- The capture prescaler is not used for triggering and does not need to be configured.
<br>- CC1S = 01in TIMx\_CCMR1 register to select only the input capture source
<br>- CC1P = 0 and CC1NP = 0 in TIMx\_CCER register to validate the polarity (and detect rising edge only).
3. Configure the timer in trigger mode by writing SMS = 110 in TIMx\_SMCR register. Select tim\_ti1 as the input source by writing TS = 00101 in TIMx\_SMCR register.

A rising edge on tim\_ti1 enables the counter and sets the TIF flag. The counter then counts on tim\_etr\_in rising edges.

The delay between the rising edge of the tim\_etr\_in signal and the actual reset of the counter is due to the resynchronization circuit on tim\_etrp input.

#### Figure 384. Control circuit in external clock mode 2 + trigger mode![](MSv62364V1.svg)

**Note:**

The clock of the slave peripherals (such as timer, ADC) receiving the tim\_trgo or the tim\_trgo2 signals must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and the clock frequency (prescaler) must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.

<a id="XREF_19651__1_4_18_Timer_synchronization21"></a>

### 29.3.31 ADC triggers

The timer can generate an ADC triggering event with various internal signals, such as reset, enable or compare events. It is also possible to generate a pulse issued by internal edge detectors, such as:

- Rising and falling edges of OC4ref
- Rising edge on OC5ref or falling edge on OC6ref

The triggers are issued on the tim\_trgo2 internal line which is redirected to the ADC. There is a total of 16 possible events, which can be selected using the MMS2[3:0] bits in the TIMx\_CR2 register.

An example of an application for 3-phase motor drives is given in [Figure 338](#XREF_80227__Figure_38__3-phase_combined_PWM_signals_with_multiple_trigger_pulses_per_period21).

**Note:**

The clock of the slave peripherals (timer, ADC, ...) receiving the tim\_trgo or the tim\_trgo2 signals must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and the clock frequency (prescaler) must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.

The clock of the ADC must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the timer.

### 29.3.32 DMA burst mode

The TIMx timers have the capability to generate multiple DMA requests upon a single event. The main purpose is to be able to reprogram part of the timer multiple times without software overhead, but it can also be used to read several registers in a row, at regular intervals.

The DMA controller destination is unique and must point to the virtual register TIMx\_DMAR. On a given timer event, the timer launches a sequence of DMA requests (burst). Each write into the TIMx\_DMAR register is actually redirected to one of the timer registers.

The DBL[4:0] bits in the TIMx\_DCR register set the DMA burst length. The timer recognizes a burst transfer when a read or a write access is done to the TIMx\_DMAR address), i.e. the number of transfers (either in half-words or in bytes).

The DBA[4:0] bits in the TIMx\_DCR register define the DMA base address for DMA transfers (when read/write access are done through the TIMx\_DMAR address). DBA is defined as an offset starting from the address of the TIMx\_CR1 register:

Example:

00000: TIMx\_CR1

00001: TIMx\_CR2

00010: TIMx\_SMCR

As an example, the timer DMA burst feature is used to update the contents of the CCRx registers (x = 2, 3, 4) upon an update event, with the DMA transferring half words into the CCRx registers.

This is done in the following steps:

1. Configure the corresponding DMA channel as follows:
<br>- DMA channel peripheral address is the DMAR register address.
<br>- DMA channel memory address is the address of the buffer in the RAM containing the data to be transferred by DMA into CCRx registers.
<br>- Number of data to transfer = 3 (see note below).
<br>- Circular mode disabled.
2. Configure the DCR register by configuring the DBA and DBL bitfields as follows:
  DBL = 3 transfers, DBA = 0xE.
3. Enable the TIMx update DMA request (set the UDE bit in the DIER register).
4. Enable TIMx.
5. Enable the DMA channel.

This example is for the case where every CCRx register to be updated once. If every CCRx register is to be updated twice for example, the number of data to transfer must be 6. Let’s take the example of a buffer in the RAM containing data1, data2, data3, data4, data5, and data6. The data is transferred to the CCRx registers as follows: on the first update DMA request, data1 is transferred to CCR2, data2 is transferred to CCR3, data3 is transferred to CCR4 and on the second update DMA request, data4 is transferred to CCR2, data5 is transferred to CCR3, and data6 is transferred to CCR4.

**Note:**

A null value can be written to the reserved registers.

### 29.3.34 Debug mode

When the microcontroller enters debug mode (Cortex®-M4 with FPU core halted), the TIMx counter can either continue to work normally or stop, depending on DBG\_TIMx\_STOP configuration bit in DBG module.

The behavior in debug mode can be programmed with a dedicated configuration bit per timer in the Debug support (DBG) module.

For safety purposes, when the counter is stopped, the outputs are disabled (as if the MOE bit was reset). The outputs can either be forced to an inactive state (OSSI bit = 1), or have their control taken over by the GPIO controller (OSSI bit = 0), typically to force a Hi-Z.

For more details, refer to section Debug support (DBG).

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.77px"/><col width="496.81px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="72.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DITHEN</span>: Dithering enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Dithering disabled<br/>1: Dithering enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The DITHEN bit can only be modified when CEN bit is reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UIFREMAP</span>: UIF status bit remapping</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No remapping. UIF status bit is not copied to TIMx_CNT register bit 31.<br/>1: Remapping enabled. UIF status bit is copied to TIMx_CNT register bit 31.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="129.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CKD[1:0]</span>: Clock division</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield indicates the division ratio between the timer clock (tim_ker_ck) frequency and the dead-time and sampling clock (t<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">DTS</span></sub>)used by the dead-time generators and the digital filters (tim_etr_in, tim_tix),</p><p class="TableIndent">00: t<sub>DTS</sub> = t<sub>tim_ker_ck<br/></sub>01: t<sub>DTS</sub> = 2*t<sub>tim_ker_ck<br/></sub>10: t<sub>DTS</sub> = 4*t<sub>tim_ker_ck<br/></sub>11: Reserved, do not program this value</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ARPE</span>: Autoreload preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: TIMx_ARR register is not buffered<br/>1: TIMx_ARR register is buffered</p></td></tr><tr height="222.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 6:5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CMS[1:0]</span>: Center-aligned mode selection</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">00:   Edge-aligned mode. The counter counts up or down depending on the direction bit (DIR).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">01:   Center-aligned mode 1. The counter counts up and down alternatively. Output compare interrupt flags of channels configured in output (CCxS = 00 in TIMx_CCMRx register) are set only when the counter is counting down.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">10:   Center-aligned mode 2. The counter counts up and down alternatively. Output compare interrupt flags of channels configured in output (CCxS = 00 in TIMx_CCMRx register) are set only when the counter is counting up.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">11:   Center-aligned mode 3. The counter counts up and down alternatively. Output compare interrupt flags of channels configured in output (CCxS = 00 in TIMx_CCMRx register) are set both when the counter is counting up or down.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>It is not allowed to switch from edge-aligned mode to center-aligned mode as long as the counter is enabled (CEN = 1)</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DIR</span>: Direction</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Counter used as upcounter<br/>1: Counter used as downcounter</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is read only when the timer is configured in Center-aligned mode or Encoder mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OPM</span>: One-pulse mode</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Counter is not stopped at update event<br/>1: Counter stops counting at the next update event (clearing the bit CEN)</p></td></tr><tr height="138.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">URS</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Update request source</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to select the UEV event sources.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Any of the following events generate an update interrupt or DMA request if enabled. These events can be: </p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Counter overflow/underflow</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Setting the UG bit</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Update generation through the slave mode controller</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   Only counter overflow/underflow generates an update interrupt or DMA request if enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="169.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UDIS</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Update disable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set and cleared by software to enable/disable UEV event generation.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   UEV enabled. The Update (UEV) event is generated by one of the following events:</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Counter overflow/underflow</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Setting the UG bit</p><p class="RegTBullet2">–<span style="padding-right:16pt ;">​</span>Update generation through the slave mode controller</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : 0.00pt;">Buffered registers are then loaded with their preload values.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   UEV disabled. The Update event is not generated, shadow registers keep their value (ARR, PSC, CCRx). However the counter and the prescaler are reinitialized if the UG bit is set or if a hardware reset is received from the slave mode controller.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CEN</span>: Counter enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Counter disabled<br/>1: Counter enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>External clock, gated mode and encoder mode can work only if the CEN bit has been previously set by software. However trigger mode can set the CEN bit automatically by hardware.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.2 TIMx control register 2 (TIMx\_CR2)(x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x004

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Refer to <a href="#XREF_40016__26_3_32_ADC_synchronization" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 29.3.33</a> for requirements.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 18.43pt;">The ADSYNC must not modified when the counter is enabled (CEN bit is set).</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 27:26</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="577.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MMS2[3:0]</span>: Master mode selection 2</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits allow the information to be sent to ADC for synchronization (tim_trgo2) to be selected. The combination is as follows:</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Reset</span> - the UG bit from the TIMx_EGR register is used as trigger output (tim_trgo2). If the reset is generated by the trigger input (slave mode controller configured in reset mode), the signal on tim_trgo2 is delayed compared to the actual reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Enable</span> - the Counter Enable signal CNT_EN is used as trigger output (tim_trgo2). It is useful to start several timers at the same time or to control a window in which a slave timer is enabled. The Counter Enable signal is generated by a logic AND between the CEN control bit and the trigger input when configured in Gated mode. When the Counter Enable signal is controlled by the trigger input, there is a delay on tim_trgo2, except if the Master/Slave mode is selected (see the MSM bit description in TIMx_SMCR register).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Update</span> - the update event is selected as trigger output (tim_trgo2). For instance, a master timer can then be used as a prescaler for a slave timer.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare pulse</span> - the trigger output sends a positive pulse when the CC1IF flag is to be set (even if it was already high), as soon as a capture or compare match occurs (tim_trgo2).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc1refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo2)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc2refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo2)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc3refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo2)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc4refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo2)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc5refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo2)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc6refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo2)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare Pulse</span> - tim_oc4refc rising or falling edges generate pulses on tim_trgo2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare pulse</span> - tim_oc6refc rising or falling edges generate pulses on tim_trgo2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare pulse</span> - tim_oc4refc or tim_oc6refc rising edges generate pulses on tim_trgo2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare pulse</span> - tim_oc4refc rising or tim_oc6refc falling edges generate pulses on tim_trgo2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare pulse</span> - tim_oc5refc or tim_oc6refc rising edges generate pulses on tim_trgo2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare pulse</span> - tim_oc5refc rising or tim_oc6refc falling edges generate pulses on tim_trgo2</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The clock of the slave timer or ADC must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.</p></td></tr><tr OIS1 bit</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OIS1N</span>: Output idle state 1 (tim_oc1n output)</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_oc1n = 0 after a dead-time when MOE = 0<br/>1: tim_oc1n = 1 after a dead-time when MOE = 0</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="86.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OIS1</span>: Output idle state 1 (tim_oc1 output)</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_oc1 = 0 (after a dead-time) when MOE = 0<br/>1: tim_oc1 = 1 (after a dead-time) when MOE = 0</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TI1S</span>: tim_ti1 selection</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: The tim_ti1_in[15:0] multiplexer output is connected to tim_ti1 input</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 18.43pt;">1: tim_ti1_in[15:0], tim_ti2_in[15:0] and tim_ti3_in[15:0] multiplexers outputs are XORed and connected to the tim_ti1 input</p></td></tr><tr height="466.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 25, 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MMS[3:0]</span>: Master mode selection</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits select the information to be sent in master mode to slave timers for synchronization (tim_trgo). The combination is as follows: </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Reset</span> - the UG bit from the TIMx_EGR register is used as trigger output (tim_trgo). If the reset is generated by the trigger input (slave mode controller configured in reset mode) then the signal on tim_trgo is delayed compared to the actual reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Enable</span> - the Counter Enable signal CNT_EN is used as trigger output (tim_trgo). It is useful to start several timers at the same time or to control a window in which a slave timer is enable. The Counter Enable signal is generated by a logic AND between CEN control bit and the trigger input when configured in gated mode. When the Counter Enable signal is controlled by the trigger input, there is a delay on tim_trgo, except if the master/slave mode is selected (see the MSM bit description in TIMx_SMCR register).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Update</span> - The update event is selected as trigger output (tim_trgo). For instance a master timer can then be used as a prescaler for a slave timer.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare Pulse</span> - The trigger output send a positive pulse when the CC1IF flag is to be set (even if it was already high), as soon as a capture or a compare match occurred. (tim_trgo).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc1refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc2refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc3refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:    <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Compare</span> - tim_oc4refc signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   <span style="font-weight:Bold;">Encoder Clock output</span> - The encoder clock signal is used as trigger output (tim_trgo). This code is valid for the following SMS[3:0] values: 0001, 0010, 0011, 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101, 1110, 1111. Any other SMS[3:0] code is not allowed and may lead to unexpected behavior.</p><p class="TableIndent">Other codes reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The clock of the slave timer or ADC must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.</p></td></tr><tr height="54.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCDS</span>: Capture/compare DMA selection</p><p class="TableIndent">0: CCx DMA request sent when CCx event occurs<br/>1: CCx DMA requests sent when update event occurs</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCUS</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Capture/compare control update selection</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   When capture/compare control bits are preloaded (CCPC = 1), they are updated by setting the COMG bit only</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   When capture/compare control bits are preloaded (CCPC = 1), they are updated by setting the COMG bit or when an rising edge occurs on tim_trgi</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit acts only on channels that have a complementary output.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCPC</span>: Capture/compare preloaded control</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   CCxE, CCxNE and OCxM bits are not preloaded</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   CCxE, CCxNE and OCxM bits are preloaded, after having been written, they are updated only when a commutation event (COM) occurs (COMG bit set or rising edge detected on tim_trgi, depending on the CCUS bit).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit acts only on channels that have a complementary output.</p></td></tr></table></div>

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.59px"/><col width="496.24px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SMSPS</span>: SMS preload source</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects whether the events that triggers the SMS[3:0] bitfield transfer from preload to active</p><p class="TableIndent">0: The transfer is triggered by the Timer’s Update event<br/>1: The transfer is triggered by the Index event</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SMSPE</span>: SMS preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects whether the SMS[3:0] bitfield is preloaded</p><p class="TableIndent">0: SMS[3:0] bitfield is not preloaded<br/>1: SMS[3:0] preload is enabled</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 21:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TS[4:3]</span>: Trigger selection - bit 4:3</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to TS[2:0] description - bits 6:4</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ETP</span>: External trigger polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit selects whether tim_etr_in or tim_<span style="text-decoration: overline;">etr_in</span> is used for trigger operations </p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_etr_in is non-inverted, active at high level or rising edge.<br/>1: tim_etr_in is inverted, active at low level or falling edge.</p></td></tr><tr height="194.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ECE</span>: External clock enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables External clock mode 2. </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   External clock mode 2 disabled</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   External clock mode 2 enabled. The counter is clocked by any active edge on the tim_etrf signal.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Setting the ECE bit has the same effect as selecting external clock mode 1 with tim_trgi connected to tim_etrf (SMS = 111 and TS = 00111).</p><p class="RegTNote_">It is possible to simultaneously use external clock mode 2 with the following slave modes: reset mode, gated mode and trigger mode. Nevertheless, tim_trgi must not be connected to tim_etrf in this case (TS bits must not be 00111).<br/>If external clock mode 1 and external clock mode 2 are enabled at the same time, the external clock input is tim_etrf.</p></td></tr><tr height="129.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 13:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ETPS[1:0]</span>: External trigger prescaler</p><p class="TableIndent">External trigger signal tim_etrp frequency must be at most 1/4 of TIMxCLK frequency. A prescaler can be enabled to reduce tim_etrp frequency. It is useful when inputting fast external clocks on tim_etr_in.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Prescaler OFF<br/>01: tim_etr_in frequency divided by 2<br/>10: tim_etr_in frequency divided by 4<br/>11: tim_etr_in frequency divided by 8</p></td></tr><tr height="325.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">ETF[3:0]</span>: External trigger filter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield then defines the frequency used to sample tim_etrp signal and the length of the digital filter applied to tim_etrp. The digital filter is made of an event counter in which N consecutive events are needed to validate a transition on the output:</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   No filter, sampling is done at f<sub>DTS</sub></p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 4</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>tim_ker_ck</sub>, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/2, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/4, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 5</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 5</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 8</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MSM:</span><span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Master/slave mode</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   The effect of an event on the trigger input (tim_trgi) is delayed to allow a perfect synchronization between the current timer and its slaves (through tim_trgo). It is useful if we want to synchronize several timers on a single external event.</p></td></tr><tr height="454.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TS[2:0]:</span> Trigger selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield is combined with TS[4:3] bits.</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield selects the trigger input to be used to synchronize the counter. </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00000:   Internal Trigger 0 (tim_itr0)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00001:   Internal Trigger 1 (tim_itr1)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00010:   Internal Trigger 2 (tim_itr2)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00011:   Internal Trigger 3 (tim_itr3)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00100:   tim_ti1 Edge Detector (tim_ti1f_ed)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00101:   Filtered Timer Input 1 (tim_ti1fp1)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00110:   Filtered Timer Input 2 (tim_ti2fp2)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00111:   External Trigger input (tim_etrf)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">01000:   Internal Trigger 4 (tim_itr4)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">01001:   Internal Trigger 5 (tim_itr5)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">01010:   Internal Trigger 6 (tim_itr6)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">01011:   Internal Trigger 7 (tim_itr7)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">01100:   Internal Trigger 8 (tim_itr8)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">01101:   Internal Trigger 9 (tim_itr9)</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">01110:   Internal Trigger 10 (tim_itr10)</p><p class="TableIndent">01111: Internal trigger 11 (tim_itr11)</p><p class="TableIndent">10000: Internal trigger 12 (tim_itr12)</p><p class="TableIndent">10001: Internal trigger 13 (tim_itr13)</p><p class="TableIndent">10010: Internal trigger 14 (tim_itr14)</p><p class="TableIndent">10011: Internal trigger 15 (tim_itr15)</p><p class="TableIndent">Others: Reserved</p><p class="TableIndent">See <span data-conditional="RM0440"><a href="#XREF_52337__Table_248__TIMx_internal_trigger_connection%1121" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Table 267: Internal trigger connection</a></span> for more details on tim_itrx meaning for each Timer.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits must be changed only when they are not used (for example when SMS = 000) to avoid wrong edge detections at the transition.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_occs" height="70.67px"><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_occs"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_occs"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OCCS:</span> OCREF clear selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used to select the OCREF clear source. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_ocref_clr_int is connected to the tim_ocref_clr input <br/>1: tim_ocref_clr_int is connected to tim_etrf</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_nogpt2acv4_occs" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_nogpt2acv4_occs" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td data-conditional="_nogpt2acv4_occs" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="668.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16, 2:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SMS[3:0]:</span> Slave mode selection</p><p class="TableIndent">When external signals are selected the active edge of the trigger signal (tim_trgi) is linked to the polarity selected on the external input (refer to ETP bit in TIMx_SMCR for tim_etr_in and CCxP/CCxNP bits in TIMx_CCER register for tim_ti1fp1 and tim_ti2fp2).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   Slave mode disabled - if CEN = 1 then the prescaler is clocked directly by the internal clock.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   Quadrature encoder mode 1, x2 mode- Counter counts up/down on tim_ti1fp1 edge depending on tim_ti2fp2 level.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   Quadrature encoder mode 2, x2 mode - Counter counts up/down on tim_ti2fp2 edge depending on tim_ti1fp1 level.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   Quadrature encoder mode 3, x4 mode - Counter counts up/down on both tim_ti1fp1 and tim_ti2fp2 edges depending on the level of the other input.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   Reset mode - Rising edge of the selected trigger input (tim_trgi) reinitializes the counter and generates an update of the registers.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   Gated mode - The counter clock is enabled when the trigger input (tim_trgi) is high. The counter stops (but is not reset) as soon as the trigger becomes low. Both start and stop of the counter are controlled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   Trigger mode - The counter starts at a rising edge of the trigger tim_trgi (but it is not reset). Only the start of the counter is controlled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   External Clock mode 1 - Rising edges of the selected trigger (tim_trgi) clock the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   Combined reset + trigger mode - Rising edge of the selected trigger input (tim_trgi) reinitializes the counter, generates an update of the registers and starts the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   Combined gated + reset mode - The counter clock is enabled when the trigger input (tim_trgi) is high. The counter stops and is reset) as soon as the trigger becomes low. Both start and stop of the counter are controlled.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   Encoder mode: Clock plus direction, x2 mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   Encoder mode: Clock plus direction, x1 mode, tim_ti2fp2 edge sensitivity is set by CC2P</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   Encoder mode: Directional Clock, x2 mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101:   Encoder mode: Directional Clock, x1 mode, tim_ti1fp1 and tim_ti2fp2 edge sensitivity is set by CC1P and CC2P.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   Quadrature encoder mode: x1 mode, counting on tim_ti1fp1 edges only, edge sensitivity is set by CC1P.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   Quadrature encoder mode: x1 mode, counting on tim_ti2fp2 edges only, edge sensitivity is set by CC2P.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The gated mode must not be used if tim_ti1f_ed is selected as the trigger input (TS = 00100). Indeed, tim_ti1f_ed outputs 1 pulse for each transition on TI1F, whereas the gated mode checks the level of the trigger signal.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The clock of the slave peripherals (timer, ADC, ...) receiving the tim_trgo or the tim_trgo2 signals must be enabled prior to receive events from the master timer, and the clock frequency (prescaler) must not be changed on-the-fly while triggers are received from the master timer.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.4 TIMx DMA/interrupt enable register (TIMx\_DIER)(x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x00C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000
