<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.50px"/><col width="495.27px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 23</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TERRF</span>: Transition error interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware when a transition error is detected in encoder mode. It is cleared by software by writing it to 0. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No encoder transition error has been detected.<br/>1: An encoder transition error has been detected</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 22</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IERRF</span>: Index error interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware when an index error is detected. It is cleared by software by writing it to 0. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No index error has been detected.<br/>1: An index error has been detected</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 21</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DIRF</span>: Direction change interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware when the direction changes in encoder mode (DIR bit value in TIMx_CR is changing). It is cleared by software by writing it to 0. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No direction change<br/>1: Direction change</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDXF</span>: Index interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware when an index event is detected. It is cleared by software by writing it to 0. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No index event occurred.<br/>1: An index event has occurred</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="57.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC6IF</span>: Compare 6 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1IF description</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Channel 6 can only be configured as output.</p></td></tr><tr height="57.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC5IF</span>: Compare 5 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1IF description</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Channel 5 can only be configured as output.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">SBIF</span>: System break interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware as soon as the system break input goes active. It can be cleared by software if the system break input is not active.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">This flag must be reset to re-start PWM operation.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No break event occurred.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   An active level has been detected on the system break input. An interrupt is generated if BIE = 1 in the TIMx_DIER register.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4OF</span>: Capture/compare 4 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1OF description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3OF</span>: Capture/compare 3 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1OF description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2OF</span>: Capture/compare 2 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1OF description</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1OF</span>: Capture/compare 1 overcapture flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware only when the corresponding channel is configured in input capture mode. It is cleared by software by writing it to 0. </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No overcapture has been detected.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   The counter value has been captured in TIMx_CCR1 register while CC1IF flag was already set</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">B2IF</span>: Break 2 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware as soon as the break 2 input goes active. It can be cleared by software if the break 2 input is not active.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No break event occurred.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   An active level has been detected on the break 2 input. An interrupt is generated if BIE = 1 in the TIMx_DIER register.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BIF</span>: Break interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware as soon as the break input goes active. It can be cleared by software if the break input is not active.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No break event occurred.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   An active level has been detected on the break input. An interrupt is generated if BIE = 1 in the TIMx_DIER register.</p></td></tr><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TIF</span>: Trigger interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware on the TRG trigger event (active edge detected on tim_trgi input when the slave mode controller is enabled in all modes but gated mode. It is set when the counter starts or stops when gated mode is selected. It is cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No trigger event occurred.<br/>1: Trigger interrupt pending.</p></td></tr><tr height="85.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">COMIF</span>: COM interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware on COM event (when capture/compare Control bits - CCxE, CCxNE, OCxM - have been updated). It is cleared by software.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No COM event occurred.<br/>1: COM interrupt pending.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4IF</span>: Capture/compare 4 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1IF description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3IF</span>: Capture/compare 3 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1IF description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2IF</span>: Capture/compare 2 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1IF description</p></td></tr><tr height="221.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1IF</span>: Capture/compare 1 interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This flag is set by hardware. It is cleared by software (input capture or output compare mode) or by reading the TIMx_CCR1 register (input capture mode only).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No compare match / No input capture occurred</p><p class="TableIndent">1: A compare match or an input capture occurred</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output</span>: this flag is set when the content of the counter TIMx_CNT matches the content of the TIMx_CCR1 register. When the content of TIMx_CCR1 is greater than the content of TIMx_ARR, the CC1IF bit goes high on the counter overflow (in up-counting and up/down-counting modes) or underflow (in downcounting mode). There are 3 possible options for flag setting in center-aligned mode, refer to the CMS bits in the TIMx_CR1 register for the full description.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input</span>: this bit is set when counter value has been captured in TIMx_CCR1 register (an edge has been detected on IC1, as per the edge sensitivity defined with the CC1P and CC1NP bits setting, in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="181.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UIF</span>: Update interrupt flag</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by hardware on an update event. It is cleared by software. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No update occurred.<br/>1: Update interrupt pending. This bit is set by hardware when the registers are updated:</p><li class="TableBullet" id="1020043" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–At overflow or underflow regarding the repetition counter value (update if repetition counter = 0) and if the UDIS = 0 in the TIMx_CR1 register.</li><li class="TableBullet" id="1020044" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–When CNT is reinitialized by software using the UG bit in TIMx_EGR register, if URS = 0 and UDIS = 0 in the TIMx_CR1 register.</li><li class="TableBullet" id="1020047" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–When CNT is reinitialized by a trigger event (refer to <a href="#XREF_35064__20_4_3_TIM1/TIM8_slave_mode_control_register_(TIMx_SMCR)21" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 29.6.3: TIMx slave mode control register (TIMx_SMCR)(x = 1, 8, 20)</a>), if URS = 0 and UDIS = 0 in the TIMx_CR1 register.</li></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.6 TIMx event generation register (TIMx\_EGR)(x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x014

Reset value: 0x0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.79px"/><col width="497.21px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:9</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">B2G</span>: Break 2 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   A break 2 event is generated. MOE bit is cleared and B2IF flag is set. Related interrupt can occur if enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BG</span>: Break generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   A break event is generated. MOE bit is cleared and BIF flag is set. Related interrupt or DMA transfer can occur if enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="101.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">TG</span>: Trigger generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   The TIF flag is set in TIMx_SR register. Related interrupt or DMA transfer can occur if enabled.</p></td></tr><tr height="89.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">COMG</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Capture/compare control update generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can be set by software, it is automatically cleared by hardware</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action</p><p class="TableIndent">1: CCxE, CCxNE and OCxM bits update (providing CCPC bit is set)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit acts only on channels having a complementary output.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4G</span>: Capture/compare 4 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1G description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3G</span>: Capture/compare 3 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1G description</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2G</span>: Capture/compare 2 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to CC1G description</p></td></tr><tr height="173.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1G</span>: Capture/compare 1 generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is set by software in order to generate an event, it is automatically cleared by hardware. </p><p class="TableIndent">0: No action<br/>1: A capture/compare event is generated on channel 1:<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output:<br/></span>CC1IF flag is set, Corresponding interrupt or DMA request is sent if enabled.<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input:<br/></span>The current value of the counter is captured in TIMx_CCR1 register. The CC1IF flag is set, the corresponding interrupt or DMA request is sent if enabled. The CC1OF flag is set if the CC1IF flag was already high.</p></td></tr><tr height="116.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">UG</span>: Update generation</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can be set by software, it is automatically cleared by hardware.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   No action</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   Reinitialize the counter and generates an update of the registers. Note that the prescaler counter is cleared too (anyway the prescaler ratio is not affected). The counter is cleared if the center-aligned mode is selected or if DIR = 0 (upcounting), else it takes the autoreload value (TIMx_ARR) if DIR = 1 (downcounting).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.7 TIMx capture/compare mode register 1 (TIMx\_CCMR1)    (x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x018

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for input capture mode (this section) or for output compare mode (next section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).

This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC2S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC2E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="325.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC1F[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Input capture 1 filter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the frequency used to sample tim_ti1 input and the length of the digital filter applied to tim_ti1. The prescaler is reset as soon as CC1E = 0 (TIMx_CCER register). </p><p class="TableIndent">00: no prescaler, capture is done each time an edge is detected on the capture input<br/>01: capture is done once every 2 events<br/>10: capture is done once every 4 events<br/>11: capture is done once every 8 events</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1S[1:0]</span>: Capture/compare 1 Selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">00:   CC1 channel is configured as output</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">01:   CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti1</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">10:   CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">11:   CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC1S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC1E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.8 TIMx capture/compare mode register 1 [alternate]    (TIMx\_CCMR1)(x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x018

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for output compare mode (this section) or for input capture mode (previous section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 1 in input capture mode and channel 2 in output compare mode).

Output compare mode:

 


<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.41px"/><col width="495.21px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2CE:</span> Output compare 2 clear enable</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 24, 14:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 2 mode</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2PE</span>: Output compare 2 preload enable</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC2FE</span>: Output compare 2 fast enable</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC2S[1:0]</span>: Capture/compare 2 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">00:   CC2 channel is configured as output</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">01:   CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">10:   CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_ti1</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">11:   CC2 channel is configured as input, tim_ic2 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through the TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC2S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC2E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1CE:</span> Output compare 1 clear enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0: tim_oc1ref is not affected by the tim_ocref_clr_int signal</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1: tim_oc1ref is cleared as soon as a High level is detected on tim_ocref_clr_int signal (tim_ocref_clr input or tim_etrf input)</p></td></tr><tr height="846.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16, 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 1 mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the behavior of the output reference signal tim_oc1ref from which tim_oc1 and tim_oc1n are derived. tim_oc1ref is active high whereas tim_oc1 and tim_oc1n active level depends on CC1P and CC1NP bits.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   Frozen - The comparison between the output compare register TIMx_CCR1 and the counter TIMx_CNT has no effect on the outputs.This mode can be used when the timer serves as a software timebase. When the frozen mode is enabled during timer operation, the ouput keeps the state (active or inactive) it had before entering the frozen state.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   Set channel 1 to active level on match. tim_oc1ref signal is forced high when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 1 (TIMx_CCR1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   Set channel 1 to inactive level on match. tim_oc1ref signal is forced low when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 1 (TIMx_CCR1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   Toggle - tim_oc1ref toggles when TIMx_CNT = TIMx_CCR1.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   Force inactive level - tim_oc1ref is forced low.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   Force active level - tim_oc1ref is forced high.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   PWM mode 1 - In upcounting, channel 1 is active as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR1 else inactive. In downcounting, channel 1 is inactive (tim_oc1ref = 0) as long as TIMx_CNT&gt;TIMx_CCR1 else active (tim_oc1ref = 1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   PWM mode 2 - In upcounting, channel 1 is inactive as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR1 else active. In downcounting, channel 1 is active as long as TIMx_CNT&gt;TIMx_CCR1 else inactive.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   Retrigerrable<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;"> </span>OPM mode 1 - In up-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   Retrigerrable<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;"> </span>OPM mode 2 - In up-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 2 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   Reserved,</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   Reserved,</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   Combined PWM mode 1 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 1. tim_oc1refc is the logical OR between tim_oc1ref and tim_oc2ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101:   Combined PWM mode 2 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 2. tim_oc1refc is the logical AND between tim_oc1ref and tim_oc2ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   Asymmetric PWM mode 1 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 1. tim_oc1refc outputs tim_oc1ref when the counter is counting up, tim_oc2ref when it is counting down.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   Asymmetric PWM mode 2 - tim_oc1ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 2. tim_oc1refc outputs tim_oc1ref when the counter is counting up, tim_oc2ref when it is counting down.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In PWM mode, the OCREF level changes when the result of the comparison changes, when the output compare mode switches from “frozen” mode to “PWM” mode and when the output compare mode switches from “force active/inactive” mode to “PWM” mode.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>On channels having a complementary output, this bitfield is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIMx_CR2 register then the OC1M active bits take the new value from the preloaded bits only when a COM event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="117.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1PE</span>: Output compare 1 preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Preload register on TIMx_CCR1 disabled. TIMx_CCR1 can be written at anytime, the new value is taken in account immediately.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   Preload register on TIMx_CCR1 enabled. Read/Write operations access the preload register. TIMx_CCR1 preload value is loaded in the active register at each update event.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p></td></tr><tr height="174.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC1FE</span>: Output compare 1 fast enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit decreases the latency between a trigger event and a transition on the timer output. It must be used in one-pulse mode (OPM bit set in TIMx_CR1 register), to have the output pulse starting as soon as possible after the starting trigger.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   CC1 behaves normally depending on counter and CCR1 values even when the trigger is ON. The minimum delay to activate CC1 output when an edge occurs on the trigger input is 5 clock cycles.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   An active edge on the trigger input acts like a compare match on CC1 output. Then, OC is set to the compare level independently from the result of the comparison. Delay to sample the trigger input and to activate CC1 output is reduced to 3 clock cycles. OCFE acts only if the channel is configured in PWM1 or PWM2 mode.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1S[1:0]</span>: Capture/compare 1 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC1 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti1<br/>10: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_ti2<br/>11: CC1 channel is configured as input, tim_ic1 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC1S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC1E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.9 TIMx capture/compare mode register 2 (TIMx\_CCMR2)    (x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x01C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for input capture mode (this section) or for output compare mode (next section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 3 in input capture mode and channel 4 in output compare mode).

Input capture mode

 


<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.50px"/><col width="494.03px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC4F[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Input capture 4 filter</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 11:10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC4PSC[1:0]</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Input capture 4 prescaler</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4S[1:0]</span>: Capture/compare 4 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC4 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_ti4<br/>10: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_ti3<br/>11: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC4S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC4E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC3F[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Input capture 3 filter</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 3:2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IC3PSC[1:0]</span>:<span style="font-style:Italic;"> </span>Input capture 3 prescaler</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3S[1:0]</span>: Capture/compare 3 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC3 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_ti3<br/>10: CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_ti4<br/>11: CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC3S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC3E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.10 TIMx capture/compare mode register 2 [alternate]    (TIMx\_CCMR2)(x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x01C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

The same register can be used for output compare mode (this section) or for input capture mode (previous section). The direction of a channel is defined by configuring the corresponding CCxS bits. All the other bits of this register have a different function for input capture and for output compare modes. It is possible to combine both modes independently (for example channel 3 in input capture mode and channel 4 in output compare mode).

Output compare mode

 


<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.68px"/><col width="497.85px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC4CE</span>: Output compare 4 clear enable</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 24, 14:12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC4M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 4 mode</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to OC3M[3:0] bit description</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC4PE</span>: Output compare 4 preload enable</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC4FE</span>: Output compare 4 fast enable</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC4S[1:0]</span>: Capture/compare 4 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent">00: CC4 channel is configured as output<br/>01: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_ti4<br/>10: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_ti3<br/>11: CC4 channel is configured as input, tim_ic4 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC4S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC4E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 7</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC3CE:</span> Output compare 3 clear enable</p></td></tr><tr height="817.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 16, 6:4</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC3M[3:0]</span>: Output compare 3 mode</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits define the behavior of the output reference signal tim_oc3ref from which tim_oc3 and tim_oc3n are derived. tim_oc3ref is active high whereas tim_oc3 and tim_oc3n active level depends on CC3P and CC3NP bits.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0000:   Frozen - The comparison between the output compare register TIMx_CCR3 and the counter TIMx_CNT has no effect on the outputs.(this mode is used to generate a timing base).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0001:   Set channel 3 to active level on match. tim_oc3ref signal is forced high when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 3 (TIMx_CCR3).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0010:   Set channel 3 to inactive level on match. tim_oc3ref signal is forced low when the counter TIMx_CNT matches the capture/compare register 3 (TIMx_CCR3).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0011:   Toggle - tim_oc3ref toggles when TIMx_CNT = TIMx_CCR3.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0100:   Force inactive level - tim_oc3ref is forced low.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0101:   Force active level - tim_oc3ref is forced high.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0110:   PWM mode 1 - In upcounting, channel 3 is active as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR3 else inactive. In downcounting, channel 3 is inactive (tim_oc3ref = 0) as long as TIMx_CNT&gt;TIMx_CCR3 else active (tim_oc3ref = 1).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">0111:   PWM mode 2 - In upcounting, channel 3 is inactive as long as TIMx_CNT&lt;TIMx_CCR3 else active. In downcounting, channel 3 is active as long as TIMx_CNT&gt;TIMx_CCR3 else inactive.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1000:   Retrigerrable<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;"> </span>OPM mode 1 - In up-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   Retrigerrable<span style="font-size : 10.00pt;"> </span>OPM mode 2 - In up-counting mode, the channel is inactive until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 2 and the channels becomes inactive again at the next update. In down-counting mode, the channel is active until a trigger event is detected (on tim_trgi signal). Then, a comparison is performed as in PWM mode 1 and the channels becomes active again at the next update.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   Pulse on compare: a pulse is generated on tim_oc3ref upon CCR3 match event, as per PWPRSC[2:0] and PW[7:0] bitfields programming in TIMxECR.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   Direction output. The tim_oc3ref signal is overridden by a copy of the DIR bit.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   Combined PWM mode 1 - tim_oc3ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 1. tim_oc3refc is the logical OR between tim_oc3ref and tim_oc4ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101: Combined PWM mode 2 - tim_oc3ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 2. tim_oc3refc is the logical AND between tim_oc3ref and tim_oc4ref.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   Asymmetric PWM mode 1 - tim_oc3ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 1. tim_oc3refc outputs tim_oc3ref when the counter is counting up, tim_oc4ref when it is counting down.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   Asymmetric PWM mode 2 - tim_oc3ref has the same behavior as in PWM mode 2. tim_oc3refc outputs tim_oc3ref when the counter is counting up, tim_oc4ref when it is counting down.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>These bits can not be modified as long as LOCK level 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (the channel is configured in output).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>In PWM mode, the OCREF level changes only when the result of the comparison changes or when the output compare mode switches from “frozen” mode to “PWM” mode.</p><p class="TableBodyL">On channels having a complementary output, this bitfield is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIMx_CR2 register then the OC3M active bits take the new value from the preloaded bits only when a COM event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 3</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC3PE</span>: Output compare 3 preload enable</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OC3FE</span>: Output compare 3 fast enable</p></td></tr><tr height="136.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 1:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC3S[1:0]</span>: Capture/compare 3 selection</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the direction of the channel (input/output) as well as the used input. </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">00:   CC3 channel is configured as output</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">01:   CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_ti3</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">10:   CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_ti4</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">11:   CC3 channel is configured as input, tim_ic3 is mapped on tim_trc. This mode is working only if an internal trigger input is selected through TS bit (TIMx_SMCR register)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>CC3S bits are writable only when the channel is OFF (CC3E = 0 in TIMx_CCER).</p></td></tr></table></div>

Capture/compare 1 complementary output polarity</p><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1 channel configured as output</span>:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: tim_oc1n active high.</p><p class="TableIndent">1: tim_oc1n active low.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1 channel configured as input</span>:</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used in conjunction with CC1P to define the polarity of tim_ti1fp1 and tim_ti2fp1. Refer to CC1P description.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not writable as soon as LOCK level 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register) and CC1S = 00 (channel configured as output).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>On channels having a complementary output, this bit is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIMx_CR2 register then the CC1NP active bit takes the new value from the preloaded bit only when a Commutation event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="132.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 2</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1NE</span>: Capture/compare 1 complementary output enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   Off - tim_oc1n is not active. tim_oc1n level is then function of MOE, OSSI, OSSR, OIS1, OIS1N and CC1E bits.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   On - tim_oc1n signal is output on the corresponding output pin depending on MOE, OSSI, OSSR, OIS1, OIS1N and CC1E bits.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>On channels having a complementary output, this bit is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIMx_CR2 register then the CC1NE active bit takes the new value from the preloaded bit only when a Commutation event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="376.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1P</span>: Capture/compare 1 output polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">0: OC1 active high (output mode) / Edge sensitivity selection (input mode, see below)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: OC1 active low (output mode) / Edge sensitivity selection (input mode, see below)</p><p class="TableIndent">When CC1 channel is configured as input, both CC1NP/CC1P bits select the active polarity of TI1FP1 and TI2FP1 for trigger or capture operations.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 99.21pt;">CC1NP = 0, CC1P = 0:   non-inverted/rising edge. The circuit is sensitive to TIxFP1 rising edge (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1 is not inverted (trigger operation in gated mode or encoder mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 99.21pt;">CC1NP = 0, CC1P = 1:   inverted/falling edge. The circuit is sensitive to TIxFP1 falling edge (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1 is inverted (trigger operation in gated mode or encoder mode).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 102.05pt;">CC1NP = 1, CC1P = 1:   non-inverted/both edges/ The circuit is sensitive to both TIxFP1 rising and falling edges (capture or trigger operations in reset, external clock or trigger mode), TIxFP1is not inverted (trigger operation in gated mode). This configuration must not be used in encoder mode.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 99.21pt;">CC1NP = 1, CC1P = 0:   the configuration is reserved, it must not be used.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit is not writable as soon as LOCK level 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>On channels having a complementary output, this bit is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIMx_CR2 register then the CC1P active bit takes the new value from the preloaded bit only when a Commutation event is generated.</p></td></tr><tr height="148.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CC1E</span>: Capture/compare 1 output enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Capture mode disabled / OC1 is not active (see below)</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Capture mode enabled / OC1 signal is output on the corresponding output pin</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">When CC1 channel is configured as output</span>, the OC1 level depends on MOE, OSSI, OSSR, OIS1, OIS1N and CC1NE bits, regardless of the CC1E bits state. Refer to <a href="#XREF_94940__Table_2__Output_Control_bits_for_complementary_OCx_and_OCxN_Channels_with21" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Table 282</a> for details.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>On channels having a complementary output, this bit is preloaded. If the CCPC bit is set in the TIMx_CR2 register then the CC1E active bit takes the new value from the preloaded bit only when a Commutation event is generated.</p></td></tr></table></div>

**Note:**

The state of the external I/O pins connected to the complementary tim\_ocx and tim\_ocxn channels depends on the tim\_ocx and tim\_ocxn channel state and the GPIO registers.

### 29.6.12 TIMx counter (TIMx\_CNT)(x = 1, 8, 20)

The ARR[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="496.84px"/><tr height="180.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">REP[15:0]</span>: Repetition counter reload value</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the update rate of the compare registers (i.e. periodic transfers from preload to active registers) when preload registers are enable. It also defines the update interrupt generation rate, if this interrupt is enable.</p><p class="TableIndent">When the repetition down-counter reaches zero, an update event is generated and it restarts counting from REP value. As the repetition counter is reloaded with REP value only at the repetition update event UEV, any write to the TIMx_RCR register is not taken in account until the next repetition update event.</p><p class="TableIndent">It means in PWM mode (REP+1) corresponds to:</p><li class="TableBullet" id="1022037" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–<span style="padding-right:4pt ;">​</span>the number of PWM periods in edge-aligned mode</li><li class="TableBullet" id="1022038" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–<span style="padding-right:4pt ;">​</span>the number of half PWM period in center-aligned mode.</li></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="495.93px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="317.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR1[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 1 value</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as output</span>: CCR1 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 1 register (preload value).</p><p class="TableIndent">It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR1 register (bit OC1PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 1 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc1 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR1[15:0]. The CCR1[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR1[19:4]. The CCR1[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC1 is configured as input</span>: CR1 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 1 event (tim_ic1). The TIMx_CCR1 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value in CCR1[15:0]. The CCR1[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR1[19:4]. The CCR1[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.14px"/><col width="496.84px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="317.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR2[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 2 value</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC2 is configured as output</span>: CCR2 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 2 register (preload value).</p><p class="TableIndent">It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR1 register (bit OC2PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 2 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc2 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR2[15:0]. The CCR2[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR2[19:4]. The CCR2[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC2 is configured as input</span>: CCR2 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 2 event (tim_ic2). The TIMx_CCR2 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value in CCR2[15:0]. The CCR2[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR2[19:4]. The CCR2[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.18 TIMx capture/compare register 3 (TIMx\_CCR3)(x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x03C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.32px"/><col width="497.75px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="317.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR3[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare value</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC3 is configured as output</span>: CCR3 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 3 register (preload value).</p><p class="TableIndent">It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR2 register (bit OC3PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 3 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc3 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR3[15:0]. The CCR3[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR3[19:4]. The CCR3[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.<br/><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC3 is configured as input</span>: CCR3 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 3 event (tim_ic3). The TIMx_CCR3 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value in CCR3[15:0]. The CCR3[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR3[19:4]. The CCR3[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.19 TIMx capture/compare register 4 (TIMx\_CCR4)(x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x040

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.23px"/><col width="496.93px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="318.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR4[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare value</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC4 is configured as output</span>: CCR4 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 4 register (preload value).</p><p class="TableIndent">It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR2 register (bit OC4PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 4 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signalled on tim_oc4 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR4[15:0]. The CCR4[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR4[19:4]. The CCR4[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p><p class="TableIndent"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">If channel CC4 is configured as input</span>: CCR4 is the counter value transferred by the last input capture 4 event (tim_ic4). The TIMx_CCR4 register is read-only and cannot be programmed.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture value in CCR4[15:0]. The CCR4[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the capture in CCR4[19:4]. The CCR4[3:0] bits are reset.</p></td></tr></table></div>

**Note:**

As the bits BKBID/BK2BID/BK2P, BK2E, BK2F[3:0], BKF[3:0], AOE, BKP, BKE, OSSI, OSSR, and DTG[7:0] can be write-locked depending on the LOCK configuration, it can be necessary to configure all of them during the first write access to the TIMx\_BDTR register.

 


<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="113.32px"/><col width="499.69px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:30</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BK2BID</span>: Break2 bidirectional</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to BKBID description</p></td></tr><tr height="150.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 28</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKBID</span>: Break bidirectional</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk in input mode</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Break input tim_brk in bidirectional mode</p><p class="TableIndent">In the bidirectional mode (BKBID bit set to 1), the break input is configured both in input mode and in open drain output mode. Any active break event asserts a low logic level on the Break input to indicate an internal break event to external devices.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="40.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BK2DSRM</span>: Break2 disarm</p><p class="TableIndent">Refer to BKDSRM description</p></td></tr><tr height="134.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 26</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKDSRM</span>: Break disarm</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk is armed</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Break input tim_brk is disarmed</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is cleared by hardware when no break source is active.</p><p class="TableIndent">The BKDSRM bit must be set by software to release the bidirectional output control (open-drain output in Hi-Z state) and then be polled it until it is reset by hardware, indicating that the fault condition has disappeared.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 25</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BK2P</span>: Break 2 polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk2 is active low<br/>1: Break input tim_brk2 is active high</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="152.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BK2E</span>: Break 2 enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the complete break 2 protection, see <a href="#XREF_61467__Figure_145__Break_and_Break2_circuitry_overview21" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Figure 343: Break and Break2 circuitry overview</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break2 function disabled<br/>1: Break2 function enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The BRKIN2 must only be used with OSSR = OSSI = 1.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be modified when LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="357.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BK2F[3:0]</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Break 2 filter</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the frequency used to sample tim_brk2 input and the length of the digital filter applied to tim_brk2. font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1001:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/8, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1010:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 5</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1011:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1100:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/16, N = 8</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1101:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 5</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1110:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 6</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">1111:   f<sub><span class="Subscript" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">SAMPLING</span></sub> = f<sub>DTS</sub>/32, N = 8</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be modified when LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="174.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 15</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">MOE</span>: Main output enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is cleared asynchronously by hardware as soon as one of the break inputs is active (tim_brk or tim_brk2). It is set by software or automatically depending on the AOE bit. It is acting only on the channels which are configured in output. </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   In response to a break 2 event. OC and OCN outputs are disabled<br/>In response to a break event or if MOE is written to 0: OC and OCN outputs are disabled or forced to idle state depending on the OSSI bit.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   OC and OCN outputs are enabled if their respective enable bits are set (CCxE, CCxNE in TIMx_CCER register).<br/>See OC/OCN enable description for more details (<a href="#XREF_94197__28_6_11_TIMx_capture/compare_enable_register_(TIM1_CCER)(TIMx_CCER)(x21" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 29.6.11: TIMx capture/compare enable register (TIMx_CCER)(x = 1, 8, 20)</a>).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 14</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">AOE</span>: Automatic output enable</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   MOE can be set only by software</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   MOE can be set by software or automatically at the next update event (if none of the break inputs tim_brk and tim_brk2 is active)</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="104.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 13</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKP</span>: Break polarity</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break input tim_brk is active low<br/>1: Break input tim_brk is active high</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="134.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 12</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">BKE</span>: Break enable</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit enables the complete break protection (including all sources connected to tim_sys_brk and BKIN sources, as per <a href="#XREF_61467__Figure_145__Break_and_Break2_circuitry_overview21" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Figure 343: Break and Break2 circuitry overview</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Break function disabled<br/>1: Break function enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit cannot be modified when LOCK level 1 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>Any write operation to this bit takes a delay of 1 APB clock cycle to become effective.</p></td></tr><tr height="193.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 11</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OSSR</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Off-state selection for Run mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used when MOE = 1 on channels having a complementary output which are configured as outputs. OSSR is not implemented if no complementary output is implemented in the timer.</p><p class="TableIndent">See OC/OCN enable description for more details (<a href="#XREF_94197__28_6_11_TIMx_capture/compare_enable_register_(TIM1_CCER)(TIMx_CCER)(x21" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 29.6.11: TIMx capture/compare enable register (TIMx_CCER)(x = 1, 8, 20)</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   When inactive, OC/OCN outputs are disabled (the timer releases the output control which is taken over by the GPIO logic, which forces a Hi-Z state).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   When inactive, OC/OCN outputs are enabled with their inactive level as soon as CCxE = 1 or CCxNE = 1 (the output is still controlled by the timer).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as soon as the LOCK level 2 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="177.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 10</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">OSSI</span>:<span style="font-weight:Bold;"> </span>Off-state selection for idle mode</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit is used when MOE = 0 due to a break event or by a software write, on channels configured as outputs.<br/>See OC/OCN enable description for more details (<a href="#XREF_94197__28_6_11_TIMx_capture/compare_enable_register_(TIM1_CCER)(TIMx_CCER)(x21" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:normal;font-style:Italic;font-size : 9.00pt;font-kerning:normal;font-stretch:normal;color:#0000ff;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Section 29.6.11: TIMx capture/compare enable register (TIMx_CCER)(x = 1, 8, 20)</a>).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">0:   When inactive, OC/OCN outputs are disabled (the timer releases the output control which is taken over by the GPIO logic and which imposes a Hi-Z state). </p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;">1:   When inactive, OC/OCN outputs are first forced with their inactive level then forced to their idle level after the deadtime. The timer maintains its control over the output.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as soon as the LOCK level 2 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="224.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 9:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">LOCK[1:0]</span>: Lock configuration</p><p class="TableIndent">These bits offer a write protection against software errors.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">00:   LOCK OFF - No bit is write protected.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">01:   LOCK Level 1 = DTG bits in TIMx_BDTR register, OISx and OISxN bits in TIMx_CR2 register and BKBID/BK2BID/BKE/BKP/AOE bits in TIMx_BDTR register can no longer be written.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">10:   LOCK Level 2 = LOCK Level 1 + CC Polarity bits (CCxP/CCxNP bits in TIMx_CCER register, as long as the related channel is configured in output through the CCxS bits) as well as OSSR and OSSI bits can no longer be written.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 22.68pt;">11:   LOCK Level 3 = LOCK Level 2 + CC Control bits (OCxM and OCxPE bits in TIMx_CCMRx registers, as long as the related channel is configured in output through the CCxS bits) can no longer be written.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>The LOCK bits can be written only once after the reset. Once the TIMx_BDTR register has been written, their content is frozen until the next reset.</p></td></tr><tr height="220.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTG[7:0]</span>: Dead-time generator setup</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the duration of the dead-time inserted between the complementary outputs. DT correspond to this duration.</p><p class="TableIndent">DTG[7:5] = 0xx =&gt; DT = DTG[7:0]x t<sub>dtg</sub> with t<sub>dtg</sub> = t<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTG[7:5] = 10x =&gt; DT = (64+DTG[5:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 2xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTG[7:5] = 110 =&gt; DT = (32+DTG[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 8xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTG[7:5] = 111 =&gt; DT = (32+DTG[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 16xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>Example if T<sub>DTS</sub> = 125 ns (8 MHz), dead-time possible values are:<br/>0 to 15875 ns by 125 ns steps,<br/>16 μs to 31750 ns by 250 ns steps,<br/>32 μs to 63 μs by 1 μs steps,<br/>64 μs to 126 μs by 2 μs steps</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr></table></div>

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.72px"/><col width="498.45px"/><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 31</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">GC5C3</span>: Group channel 5 and channel 3</p><p class="TableIndent">Distortion on channel 3 output:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No effect of tim_oc5ref on tim_oc3refc</p><p class="TableIndent">1: tim_oc3refc is the logical AND of tim_oc3ref and tim_oc5ref</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can either have immediate effect or be preloaded and taken into account after an update event (if preload feature is selected in TIMxCCMR2).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>it is also possible to apply this distortion on combined PWM signals.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 30</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">GC5C2</span>: Group channel 5 and channel 2</p><p class="TableIndent">Distortion on channel 2 output:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No effect of tim_oc5ref on tim_oc2refc</p><p class="TableIndent">1: tim_oc2refc is the logical AND of tim_oc2ref and tim_oc5ref</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can either have immediate effect or be preloaded and taken into account after an update event (if preload feature is selected in TIMxCCMR1).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>it is also possible to apply this distortion on combined PWM signals.</p></td></tr><tr height="120.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 29</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">GC5C1</span>: Group channel 5 and channel 1</p><p class="TableIndent">Distortion on channel 1 output:</p><p class="TableIndent">0: No effect of oc5ref on oc1refc</p><p class="TableIndent">1: oc1refc is the logical AND of oc1ref and oc5ref</p><p class="TableIndent">This bit can either have immediate effect or be preloaded and taken into account after an update event (if preload feature is selected in TIMxCCMR1).</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>it is also possible to apply this distortion on combined PWM signals.</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 28:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="194.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR5[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 5 value</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR5 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 5 register (preload value).</p><p class="TableIndent">It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR3 register (bit OC5PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 5 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc5 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR5[15:0]. The CCR5[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR5[19:4]. The CCR5[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.22 TIMx capture/compare register 6 (TIMx\_CCR6)(x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x04C

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.72px"/><col width="498.45px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:20</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="194.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 19:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">CCR6[19:0]</span>: Capture/compare 6 value</p><p class="TableIndent">CCR6 is the value to be loaded in the actual capture/compare 6 register (preload value).</p><p class="TableIndent">It is loaded permanently if the preload feature is not selected in the TIMx_CCMR3 register (bit OC6PE). Else the preload value is copied in the active capture/compare 6 register when an update event occurs.</p><p class="TableIndent">The active capture/compare register contains the value to be compared to the counter TIMx_CNT and signaled on tim_oc6 output.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Non-dithering mode (DITHEN = 0)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the compare value in CCR6[15:0]. The CCR6[19:16] bits are reset.</p><p class="TableIndent" style="text-decoration: underline;">Dithering mode (DITHEN = 1)</p><p class="TableIndent">The register holds the integer part in CCR6[19:4]. The CCR6[3:0] bitfield contains the dithered part.</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.23 TIMx capture/compare mode register 3 (TIMx\_CCMR3)    (x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x050

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

Refer to the above CCMR1 register description. Channels 5 and 6 can only be configured in output.
