<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.72px"/><col width="498.45px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:18</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="88.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 17</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTPE</span>: Deadtime preload enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Deadtime value is not preloaded</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime value preload is enabled</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="102.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTAE</span>: Deadtime asymmetric enable</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Deadtime on rising and falling edges are identical, and defined with DTG[7:0] register</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Deadtime on rising edge is defined with DTG[7:0] register and deadtime on falling edge is defined with DTGF[7:0] bits.</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bit can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="220.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DTGF[7:0]</span>: Dead-time falling edge generator setup</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the duration of the dead-time inserted between the complementary outputs, on the falling edge.</p><p class="TableIndent">DTGF[7:5] = 0xx =&gt; DTF = DTGF[7:0]x t<sub>dtg</sub> with t<sub>dtg</sub> = t<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTGF[7:5] = 10x =&gt; DTF = (64+DTGF[5:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 2xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTGF[7:5] = 110 =&gt; DTF = (32+DTGF[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 8xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>DTGF[7:5] = 111 =&gt; DTF = (32+DTGF[4:0])xt<sub>dtg</sub> with T<sub>dtg</sub> = 16xt<sub>DTS</sub>.<br/>Example if T<sub>DTS</sub> = 125 ns (8 MHz), dead-time possible values are:<br/>0 to 15875 ns by 125 ns steps,<br/>16 μs to 31750 ns by 250 ns steps,<br/>32 μs to 63 μs by 1 μs steps,<br/>64 μs to 126 μs by 2 μs steps</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>This bitfield can not be modified as long as LOCK level 1, 2 or 3 has been programmed (LOCK bits in TIMx_BDTR register).</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="115.72px"/><col width="498.45px"/><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:27</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="70.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 26:24</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PWPRSC[2:0]</span>: Pulse width prescaler</p><p class="Body">This bitfield sets the clock prescaler for the pulse generator, as following:</p><p class="Body">t<sub>PWG</sub> = (2<sup>(PWPRSC[2:0])</sup>) x <span style="font-size : 9.00pt;">t</span><sub><span style="font-size : 9.00pt;">tim_ker_ck</span></sub></p></td></tr><tr height="64.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 23:16</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">PW[7:0]</span>: Pulse width</p><p class="TableIndent">This bitfield defines the pulse duration, as following:</p><p class="Body">t<sub>PW</sub> = PW[7:0] x t<sub>PWG</sub></p></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 15:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="233.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:6</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IPOS[1:0]</span>: Index positioning</p><p class="TableBodyL">In quadrature encoder mode (SMS[3:0] = 0001, 0010, 0011, 1110, 1111), this bit indicates in which AB input configuration the Index event resets the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Index resets the counter when AB = 00</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Index resets the counter when AB = 01</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Index resets the counter when AB = 10</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Index resets the counter when AB = 11</p><p class="TableIndent"><br/></p><p class="TableBodyL">In directional clock mode or clock plus direction mode (SMS[3:0] = 1010, 1011, 1100, 1101), these bits indicates on which level the Index event resets the counter. In bidirectional clock mode, this applies for both clock inputs.</p><p class="TableIndent">x0: Index resets the counter when clock is 0</p><p class="TableIndent">x1: Index resets the counter when clock is 1</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span>IPOS[1] bit is not significant</p></td></tr><tr height="73.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">FIDX</span>: First index </p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit indicates if the first index only is taken into account</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Index is always active</p><p class="TableIndent">1: the first Index only resets the counter</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" height="105.33px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:3</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IBLK[1:0]</span>: Index blanking</p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit indicates if the Index event is conditioned by the tim_ti3 or tim_ti4 input</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Index always active</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Index disabled when tim_ti3 input is active, as per CC3P bitfield</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Index disabled when tim_ti4 input is active, as per CC4P bitfield</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Reserved</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_0,_gpt2acv4_1" height="22.67px"><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_0,_gpt2acv4_1"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:3</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_0,_gpt2acv4_1"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="122.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 2:1</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IDIR[1:0]</span>: Index direction</p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit indicates in which direction the Index event resets the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">00: Index resets the counter whatever the direction</p><p class="TableIndent">01: Index resets the counter when up-counting only</p><p class="TableIndent">10: Index resets the counter when down-counting only</p><p class="TableIndent">11: Reserved</p><p class="RegTNote">Note:<span style="padding-right:7pt ;">​</span><span data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_0,_gpt2acv4_1">The IDR[1:0] bitfield must be written when IE bit is reset (index disabled).</span></p></td></tr><tr height="73.33px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bit 0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">IE</span>: Index enable</p><p class="TableBodyL">This bit indicates if the Index event resets the counter.</p><p class="TableIndent">0: Index disabled</p><p class="TableIndent">1: Index enabled</p></td></tr></table></div>

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.77px"/><col width="499.41px"/><tr data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_0" height="22.67px"><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_0"><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:13</p></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_0"><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_1,_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_1,_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_1,_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_1,_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" height="244.00px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_1,_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_1,_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"></td></tr><tr data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_1,_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" height="22.67px" style="display: none"><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_1,_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"></td><td data-conditional="_gpt2acv4_1,_gpt2acv4_2,_gpt2acv4_3,_gpt2acv4_4,_gpt2acv4_5,_gpt2acv5_0" style="display: none"></td></tr><tr height="354.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 12:8</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DBL[4:0]</span>: DMA burst length</p><p class="TableIndent">This 5-bit vector defines the length of DMA transfers (the timer recognizes a burst transfer when a read or a write access is done to the TIMx_DMAR address), i.e. the number of transfers. Transfers can be in half-words or in bytes (see example below).</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00000:   1 transfer</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00001:   2 transfers</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00010:   3 transfers</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">...</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">11010:   26 transfers</p><p class="TableIndent"><span class="Bold" style="font-family : Arial ; font-weight:Bold;font-style:normal;font-size : 9.00pt;text-decoration:none;font-kerning:normal;text-transform:none;font-stretch:normal;color:#000000;background-color:transparent;letter-spacing : 0.00em;">Example:</span> Let us consider the following transfer: DBL = 7 bytes &amp; DBA = TIM2_CR1.</p><li class="TableBullet" id="14843976" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–If DBL = 7 bytes and DBA = TIM2_CR1 represents the address of the byte to be transferred, the address of the transfer is given by the following equation:</li><p class="TableIndent">(TIMx_CR1 address) + DBA + (DMA index), where DMA index = DBL</p><p class="TableIndent">In this example, 7 bytes are added to (TIMx_CR1 address) + DBA, which gives us the address from/to which the data are copied. In this case, the transfer is done to 7 registers starting from the following address: (TIMx_CR1 address) + DBA</p><p class="TableIndent">According to the configuration of the DMA Data Size, several cases may occur:</p><li class="TableBullet" id="14843980" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–If the DMA Data Size is configured in half-words, 16-bit data are transferred to each of the 7 registers.</li><li class="TableBullet" id="14843981" style="margin-left : 17.01pt;text-indent : -8.50pt;">–If the DMA Data Size is configured in bytes, the data are also transferred to 7 registers: the first register contains the first MSB byte, the second register, the first LSB byte and so on. So with the transfer Timer, one also has to specify the size of data transferred by DMA.</li></td></tr><tr height="22.67px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 7:5</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL">Reserved, must be kept at reset value.</p></td></tr><tr height="148.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 4:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DBA[4:0]</span>: DMA base address</p><p class="TableIndent">This 5-bits vector defines the base-address for DMA transfers (when read/write access are done through the TIMx_DMAR address). DBA is defined as an offset starting from the address of the TIMx_CR1 register.<br/>Example:</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00000:   TIMx_CR1</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00001:   TIMx_CR2</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 39.69pt;">00010:   TIMx_SMCR</p><p class="TableIndent" style="margin-left : 34.02pt;">...</p></td></tr></table></div>


### 29.6.30 TIMx DMA address for full transfer (TIMx\_DMAR)(x = 1, 8, 20)

Address offset: 0x3E0

Reset value: 0x0000 0000

<div align="left"><table class="RegBitDef"><col width="114.64px"/><col width="499.53px"/><tr height="100.00px"><td><p class="RegTBodyR">Bits 31:0</p></td><td><p class="TableBodyL"><span style="font-weight:Bold;">DMAB[31:0]</span>: DMA register for burst accesses</p><p class="TableIndent">A read or write operation to the DMAR register accesses the register located at the address (TIMx_CR1 address) + (DBA + DMA index) x 4 </p><p class="TableIndent">where TIMx_CR1 address is the address of the control register 1, DBA is the DMA base address configured in TIMx_DCR register, DMA index is automatically controlled by the DMA transfer, and ranges from 0 to DBL (DBL configured in TIMx_DCR).</p></td></tr></table></div>
